title: Linux production control through Bitfocus Companion
scope: A separately installable Bitfocus Companion module that connects one module instance to one OverlayKit Show, exposes authorized visibility actions, and projects server-known feedback on Linux.
summary: A Linux production operator configures one Companion module instance with an OverlayKit device endpoint, secret bearer, and pinned trust bundle. After signed bootstrap and readiness, Companion exposes Show-scoped actions and feedback so one physical or virtual button can perform a production command without requiring the operator to navigate browser screens.

actors.description: Operates an OverlayKit production through Bitfocus Companion.

actors.label: Owner

actors.label: OverlayKit server

terms.name: Module Instance
terms.definition: One configured Bitfocus Companion connection that controls exactly one OverlayKit Show.

terms.name: Verified Projection
terms.definition: The latest module-visible state derived from accepted signed server evidence and transport lifecycle facts.

terms.name: DeviceTrustBundle
terms.definition: The externally obtained and explicitly pinned Ed25519 public identity used to verify OverlayKit device artifacts.

terms.name: Action Binding
terms.definition: A Show-scoped action identity learned from an admitted signed catalog and used to construct commands.

requirements.statement: One module instance controls exactly one Show learned from verified signed bootstrap.
requirements.verification: Bootstrap tests reject cross-Show catalogs, state, and commands.

requirements.statement: The module exposes stable visibility.show, visibility.hide, and visibility.toggle actions derived from current admitted action bindings.
requirements.verification: Official host action-definition and catalog replacement tests.

requirements.statement: The module projects active, inactive, unknown, disconnected, failed, and unavailable without inventing a production state.
requirements.verification: Feedback projection tests covering snapshots, deltas, failures, disconnects, and unavailable catalogs.

requirements.statement: Bearer authority is provided through Companion secrets and is never logged, exported, exposed as a variable, or accepted from URL user information, query, or fragment fields.
requirements.verification: Configuration, diagnostics, serialization, and hostile URL tests.

requirements.statement: The module requires an explicit valid DeviceTrustBundle before connecting and never fetches or replaces trust through the device WebSocket.
requirements.verification: Missing, malformed, substituted, and changed trust tests.

requirements.statement: WSS is required by default; plain WS is allowed for loopback and requires an explicit persistent warning opt-in for non-loopback endpoints.
requirements.verification: Endpoint parser and transport admission tests.

requirements.statement: The module remains not ready until a complete signed bootstrap is applied, acknowledged, and followed by device.ready.
requirements.verification: Lifecycle ordering and pre-ready command rejection tests.

requirements.statement: A command uses a fresh admitted action binding and expected revision; its acknowledgement or result does not change visibility without authoritative state evidence.
requirements.verification: Command, acknowledgement, result, revision, and delayed-delta tests.

requirements.statement: The last verified state remains projected until newer evidence arrives; disconnection, protocol failure, and unavailable authority remain distinct states.
Retryable network and server failures reconnect with bounded jittered backoff, while authorization, trust, protocol, and configuration failures remain closed until reconfiguration or restart.
requirements.verification: Deterministic scheduler and error classification tests.

requirements.statement: The module is Node 22 ESM, targets Companion Module API 2.0, and loads through the official @companion-module/host API 2.0 boundary.
requirements.verification: Engine-strict build and official host lifecycle integration test.

requirements.statement: Protocol parsing, verification, canonicalization, and admission come only from an exact packed public @overlaykit/protocol dependency.
requirements.verification: Tarball digest, dependency graph, import boundary, and hostile artifact tests.

userStories.need: control OverlayKit visibility from a Companion button
userStories.outcome: timed production actions do not require changing browser screens
preconditions: The Owner has issued a Show-scoped device credential.
The Owner has provided the matching DeviceTrustBundle through a separate authenticated path.
OverlayKit and Companion are reachable from the Linux production host.

acceptanceCriteria.given: valid endpoint, secret bearer, pinned trust, and signed bootstrap
acceptanceCriteria.then: Companion exposes the current Show actions and verified feedback
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Official host integration: configure, bootstrap, acknowledge, ready, and definition inspection.

acceptanceCriteria.given: an available visibility action with a current revision
acceptanceCriteria.when: the operator invokes show, hide, or toggle
acceptanceCriteria.then: the module sends one authorized command and changes feedback only after accepted server state evidence
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Integration: action callback, command frame, result, and signed state delta.

acceptanceCriteria.given: the connection is open but current state evidence is absent or stale
acceptanceCriteria.then: the button projects unknown or unavailable rather than a guessed active state
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Feedback tests with missing, stale, and unavailable evidence.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a retryable disconnect or a terminal trust, authorization, protocol, or configuration failure
acceptanceCriteria.then: it reconnects only for the retryable class and exposes disconnected or failed without leaking secrets
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Deterministic reconnect, status, and log-capture tests.

workflows.title: Configure and operate one OverlayKit Show
steps: The Owner provisions a Show-scoped bearer and obtains the server DeviceTrustBundle separately.
The operator configures one module instance with endpoint, secret bearer, and pinned trust.
The module validates configuration before opening the fixed device WebSocket.
The server authenticates the upgrade and sends a complete signed bootstrap.
The module verifies and applies the bootstrap, acknowledges its exact hashes, and waits for device.ready.
Companion exposes actions and feedback from the admitted catalog and state.
The operator invokes a visibility action.
The module sends a command using the current binding and expected revision.
The server returns command evidence and authoritative signed state.
The module preserves or changes feedback only as justified by the newest accepted evidence.
